declarations.description:
Base class every component extends.

Kept intentionally thin: universal resets/properties and the registration
contract only. Behavior that not every component needs (open/close, focus
delegation, form association, ...) belongs in a mixin from `src/mixins`.
Custom events are dispatched as typed `Event` subclasses from
`src/events`, not through a generic base-class `emit()` helper — see
`src/events/modal-close.ts` for the pattern.

Classes never register themselves (ADR 0001, D1): `defineComponents()`
registers a subclass per prefix (`u-button`, `acme-button`, ...) and
hands it the tag names of its registration through `tagNames`.
declarations.name: DSBaseElement

members.name: componentName

another component's tag in a template, nor create one with

Mixin: Attaches `ElementInternals` and exposes it as `this.internals`.

`attachInternals()` can only be called once per element, so any component
that needs form participation (`internals.form`, `setFormValue`, validity)
or `:state()` custom states should apply this mixin and read `this.internals`

Wraps `internals.states` so components can toggle `:state(x)` selectors
(e.g. `:state(open)`) instead of reflecting extra boolean attributes.

`:state()` styling must stay an enhancement — reflect an attribute too
when the state is needed for the component to look right.

declarations.description:
An alert component that displays a message to the user.

The icon of its type comes first: the icon of the same name, from the
`icon` component of its registration. It's decorative: the type is in the
role and the colors, and the message says it.

Its container is a live region (`role="status"` or `"alert"`, from
`type`). Screen readers announce what is added to a live region, not what
it already held when it appeared, so the message is revealed 100 ms after
the alert is first rendered: an alert inserted with its message is
announced too. Until then the message is laid out (nothing moves) but
invisible.

declarations.description:
Shared base of the form fields, `text-field` and `textarea`: a label, an
optional hint, a native control and its error message. Abstract: extend
`TextField` or `Textarea`, or write a field with `renderControl()`. The
label stays in the shadow root of its control: an `id` doesn't cross a
shadow root (ADR 0007).

A field takes part in its form like a native control: it submits `value`
under `name`, blocks the submission while invalid, follows the form's
reset and a `<fieldset disabled>`.

Validation is the browser's, on the native control, plus
`setCustomValidity()`. The error shows once the user has changed the value
and left the field, or once validation has run (a submission attempt,
`checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`), then follows each keystroke. The
message is the browser's, in the browser's language: give `error-message`
to write it in the page's language. A message set with
`setCustomValidity()` comes first.

Its `input` and `change` events are those of a native control, on the
host: frameworks bind `value` as they would on an `<input>` (`v-model` in
Vue).
declarations.name: FieldBase

`controlInvalid`, `controlDescribedBy`, `handleInput` and

declarations.description:
An icon of the set of its registration, by name (ADR 0005).

The set of the base is `@unicorne/icons`: one module per icon, loaded the
first time an icon renders, so a page downloads only the icons it shows.
The box keeps its size while the icon loads, and `updateComplete` resolves
once the icon is rendered. The icon takes the color of the text
(`currentColor`).

Without `label`, the icon is decorative: assistive technologies ignore it.
Give a `label` to an icon that carries meaning on its own.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description:
Whether the modal is open. Reflects to the `open` attribute, so it can
be set declaratively (`<u-modal open>`) or bound reactively
(`?open=${state}`) — the underlying `<dialog>` is kept in sync in
`updated()`. Reading `.open` always reflects the real dialog state,
including when the user closes it via Escape.

attributes.name: label

dialog without a name is announced as just "dialog".

attributes.name: close-label
attributes.description: Accessible label of the built-in close button.

members.name: componentName
members.description:
Name of the component in the catalog, without any tag prefix: the
registered tag is `<prefix>-<componentName>`. Every concrete component
sets it; abstract bases (e.g. `ButtonBase`) don't.

members.name: type
members.description: Type of the input: `text`, `email`, `password`, `tel`, `url` or `search`.

members.name: minLength
members.description: Minimum length of the value, in characters.

members.name: maxLength
members.description: Maximum length of the value, in characters: the input stops there.

members.name: pattern
members.description: A regular expression the whole value must match.

members.name: renderControl
members.description:
Renders the native control, between the hint and the error message. It
has `id="control"` (the label's `for`), `class="control"` (the styles)
and its own part. It binds `.value=${live(this.value)}`, `required`,
`disabled` (`isDisabled`), `autocomplete`, its constraints,
`controlInvalid`, `controlDescribedBy`, `handleInput` and
`handleChange`.

members.name: customStates
members.default: { set: (name: string, active: boolean) => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return; } if (active) { this.internals.states.add(name); } else { this.internals.states.delete(name); } }, has: (name: string): boolean => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return false; } return this.internals.states.has(name); }, }
members.description:
Wraps `internals.states` so components can toggle `:state(x)` selectors
(e.g. `:state(open)`) instead of reflecting extra boolean attributes.
A no-op where `:state()` is unsupported (see `supportsCustomStates`), so
`:state()` styling must stay an enhancement — reflect an attribute too
when the state is needed for the component to look right.

members.name: setCustomValidity

check of the application, such as a username already taken. `""` makes
